title: Chili Mac Skillet
subtitle: Two cravings, one pan
description: Two cravings, one pan. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Dice and open cans
steps.instruction: Dice onions and peppers ¼ inch. Drain beans. Open tomatoes. Set out your largest stock pot — chili splatters, so have a lid nearby.

steps.title: Brown the meat hard
steps.instruction: Brown beef in batches over medium-high until deeply colored (160°F+). Don't crowd the pot or you'll steam gray meat.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.instruction: Add vegetables; cook 6–8 minutes. Stir in garlic, chili powder, and paprika 45 seconds until fragrant. Add tomatoes, broth, and beans.

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.instruction: Simmer uncovered 35–45 minutes at a gentle bubble until a spoon dragged through leaves a clear trail. Taste for salt — chili should be bold, not flat.

steps.title: Hold for the hall
steps.instruction: Keep on low or in a cambro for late eaters. Topping bar: cheese, onion, jalapeños, sour cream. First bowl is best; stir before each refill.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Chili Mac Skillet with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chili Mac Skillet on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Two cravings, one pan. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
